## RULING 162 — a bypass is only as safe as the paths it can carry

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-25*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/shipping-ci.md`.


**A scheduled workflow that pushes to `main` declares which paths it may write,
and the shared pusher refuses anything else. Fail closed, per workflow, with no
skip flag.**

*The rationale stays attached, because a stripped rule reads as guidance.*
Hardening `main` on 2026-08-25 blocked all eight scheduled pushers, which push
directly. Sean ruled for a scoped bypass for the Actions bot — and **a bypass
that could carry code is the 8/25 hole reopened.** That hole was sessions
merging red code through PRs with nothing required; the actor was Claude Code
and the payload was code. The allowlist is what makes the payload structurally
incapable of being code, which is the only reason the bypass is acceptable at
all.

- **PER-WORKFLOW, not one global list.** A single list is the union of eight
  workflows' needs, so the FEC refresher would be permitted to write the ballot.
  Each profile grants exactly what its own workflow writes, so the blast radius
  of any one of them is one artifact.
- **It fails closed in FOUR directions**: an unknown or absent workflow id, a
  diff that could not be read, an **empty** diff, and any path outside the
  profile. The empty case is the one that looks harmless — a push of nothing is
  a path check with nothing to check, which is RULING 159's earned zero.
- **A second, independent list bars the dangerous prefixes outright**, so a
  profile widened by mistake still cannot admit `.github/`, `scripts/`, `lib/`,
  `tests/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/rulings.md` or the resolved tracker store.
  Re-deriving one list from the other would prove the file equals itself
  (RULING 147).
- **It lives in `scripts/push-main.mjs`**, the one script all eight already go
  through. Eight copies of a guard is eight places for it to drift, and a ninth
  pusher would inherit the copy nobody remembered to add.

**THE LIST IS DERIVED FROM WHAT THE PUSHERS ACTUALLY WRITE**, read off their own
`git add` lines, never from what they were expected to write. That reading is
what produced the finding: **`job-watch` ran `git add docs/` — the whole
directory — while needing exactly one file in it.** `docs/` holds `rulings.md`,
the resolved tracker store and every generated report, so anything left dirty in
the runner's tree by an earlier step would have been swept into a bot commit and
pushed to `main` unreviewed. Nothing had gone wrong yet; the blast radius was
simply far larger than the job's purpose.

**One grant sits outside `data/` and it is named rather than absorbed.**
`job-watch` may write `docs/tracker-working.csv`, because RULING 56 makes
committing the Needs Sean row its entire function, and that row is the only
channel that reaches a person when a scheduled job fails twice running. The
brief said the allowlist never includes the tracker stores; read strictly that
ends the alarm. The grant is made to one workflow for one file, reported, and
rowed for Sean to overrule (`NH204`).

`lib/ops/push-allowlist.ts`, guarded in `tests/push-allowlist.test.ts`, whose
load-bearing case is a workflow that did not exist when the guard was written:
a guardless pusher is constructed, caught, and gone when the test ends
(RULING 157).

## RULING 163 — the answer to "is the protection still what we think" is a command

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.


**Branch protection is asserted against the live API by `pnpm protection:verify`,
which exits non-zero on drift and on could-not-tell.**

*The rationale.* `main` was hardened by hand and read back once, into a ruling,
as a table. **A table in a document is a claim about a server on the day
somebody looked.** Protection is edited in a web UI by a person, under no diff
and no review, and nothing in this repo would have noticed a checkbox coming
off — which is how the 8/25 chain started.

- **`cannot-tell` is not a pass** and exits `2`. No credential is not a pass
  (RULING 24, RULING 125).
- **It understands classic protection AND rulesets**, because the scoped bypass
  moves `main` from one to the other and a verifier that knew only the shape it
  was written against would report `cannot-tell` on the day it is most wanted.
  It reports `shape: both`, which is the trap: the two are **additive**, so
  leaving classic in place means the bot is still refused while the ruleset
  looks correct.
- **It closes the half of RULING 156 that no ruleset existed for.** That ruling
  anchors the required-context names against `build-check.yml` and fails in both
  directions; it cannot see a name registered on a *branch*. Moving to a ruleset
  re-registers all three names BY HAND, which is exactly when a typo enters. A
  context spelled `gates (test, lint, tsc)` reads as MISSING, never as
  agreement.
- **It is STANDALONE, not in `pnpm gates`**, and the reason is stated rather
  than assumed: it needs `gh` authenticated with admin scope, which reading
  branch protection requires and which the gates job — running with
  `contents: read` — has neither.

`lib/ops/protection-state.ts` holds the judgement with no network in it, so the
intended end state is testable and was pinned in `tests/protection-state.test.ts`
**before it existed on the server**, which is the only way a click-list can be
checked against anything.

## RULING 164 — a workflow reports every failure, not just the first

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/shipping-ci.md`.


**Independent steps run to completion and report together. A genuinely
dependent step says "stopped here, N not attempted" rather than letting a
skipped step read as a passing one. And a `continue-on-error` step whose
outcome nobody reads is a swallowed failure.**

*The rationale.* Three failures were once stacked in run order in this repo,
each invisible until the one before it was fixed. **A workflow that reports only
its first failure makes the number of remaining defects unbounded** — nobody can
know how many lie between the current failure and the end, so every fix costs
another round trip through CI. It is the same family as every instrument defect
this repo has named: a mechanism reporting less than it knows.

*Measured on adoption: 9 workflows audited, 3 short-circuiting on independent
steps and 3 fixed, 6 legitimately dependent with the reason stated.*

- **`intake-tripwire`** ran three independent checks unguarded and in sequence —
  the schema gate, the write alarm and the tripwire — so the first failure ended
  the job. A schema that has drifted is precisely when the write alarm is most
  worth reading, so letting the gate suppress it is the wrong way round.
- **`refresh-daily`**'s go-red-for-failed-sources step lacked `always()`, so a
  validation failure hid which sources had failed. **Its sibling in
  `refresh-meetings-snapshot` already carried the guard** — an independent case,
  and the one that proves the correct form (RULING 157).
- **`refresh-nj-filing`** carried `continue-on-error: true` on the clerk-count
  reconciliation with **nothing reading `steps.pair.outcome` afterwards**, so a
  disagreement between the clerk's published count and what we render was
  swallowed whole and the run finished green. It stays non-blocking, as
  designed, and becomes visible.

**The general rule is the third one, and it is the class rather than the
instance** (RULING 136): `continue-on-error` converts a failure into a silent
pass, so any step carrying it must have its outcome read by something
downstream. `tests/workflow-failure-reporting.test.ts` sweeps every workflow for
it, asserts a floor so a reader that matched nothing cannot report green
(RULING 159), and is shown catching a planted one.

## RULING 165 — the scheduled pushers authenticate as a deploy key, and the private half is never held

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/shipping-ci.md`.


**What this replaces, and why.** RULING 162 built a per-workflow path allowlist
to make a scoped bypass safe, on the assumption that the bypass would be granted
to the GitHub Actions app. **It cannot be.** A branch ruleset's `Add bypass`
list does not offer GitHub Actions as a selectable actor — confirmed by Sean
against the live UI on 2026-08-26, Apps tab filtered on `actions`, zero
suggestions. The community reports were right and the documentation was not.

So the bypass is granted to the **Deploy keys** category, and the eight
scheduled pushers stop using the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` over HTTPS.

**The cutover is in `scripts/push-main.mjs` and `lib/ops/deploy-key-ssh.ts`, and
nowhere else.** All eight pushers already routed through that one script. Eight
edits in eight workflows would be eight places to drift, and a ninth pusher
would inherit whichever copy nobody updated. *The one thing that could not live
there is the secret REFERENCE — `${{ secrets.* }}` is only expressible in
workflow YAML — so each pusher carries one plumbing line, and a test asserts all
eight carry it against a stated denominator, which turns eight lines into a
guarded invariant rather than eight places to drift.*

**Two facts about the bypass make the allowlist matter more than it did
yesterday, not less.**

- **It is CATEGORY-WIDE.** `bypass_actors` reports `DeployKey` with
  `actor_id: null`; there is no way to name a single key. Every write-enabled
  deploy key on the repository holds it. One is the intended state, and
  `pnpm protection:verify` now counts them and goes red at two.
- **Its mode is `exempt`, and that is Sean's settled decision.** An `always`
  bypass still EVALUATES the ruleset and waves the actor through afterward;
  `exempt` skips enforcement outright, which is what GitHub recommends for
  trusted high-volume automation and what a scheduled deploy-key push is. The
  consequence is stated rather than left implied: **an exempt key skips every
  rule in the ruleset, not only the ones that were blocking it. There is nothing
  left on the server between a scheduled job and `main`.**
  `lib/ops/push-allowlist.ts` is the whole of it, and it is unchanged and
  unweakened by this cutover.

**THE CREDENTIAL RULE SHAPED EVERY DESIGN DECISION, and it is absolute.** On
2026-08-25 a `curl` reporting flag printed nine credential values into a
transcript that mirrors to Drive, and all nine required rotation (RULING 127). A
private key is that failure with a worse blast radius. So:

- **No private key is generated, printed, echoed, or written by any session.**
  Sean generates the keypair locally, puts the public half in Deploy keys and
  the private half in the `PUSH_DEPLOY_KEY` secret. Code references the secret
  by name and never reads its value. **A design that would require a session to
  hold the private key is a wrong design and is changed.**
- **No diagnostic may carry key material.** Every refusal describes the key's
  SHAPE — absent, empty, missing its header, public half pasted by mistake — and
  the test proves it by handing in a marker and asserting it does not come back
  out.
- **The key file never lands in the repository or a synced folder.**
  `refuseUnsafeKeyRoot` turns that from a habit into a check, refusing rather
  than silently relocating.
- **It is removed on every exit path, the failure path included** — a `finally`
  around the push loop, proved through a declared seam because the real path
  needs a private key and a network call.
- **Even the tests hold no key.** A structural placeholder exercises every
  decision the module makes, which are all about shape and placement. Generating
  a throwaway keypair to make a test feel more real would put private-key
  material into a test run, a temp folder and a CI log.

**HOST VERIFICATION IS PINNED, NEVER DISABLED.** The obvious way to make an
unattended SSH push work is `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`, and that turns every
push into an unauthenticated one. `GITHUB_HOST_KEYS` is a DECLARED constant read
from GitHub's own `meta` endpoint — a value fetched at push time from the host
you are about to authenticate is not verification, it is a round trip. *Verified
against the live endpoint on adoption: `ssh -T git@github.com` with only these
keys pinned and no identity offered returned `Permission denied (publickey)`,
which means host verification SUCCEEDED and only authentication failed. A wrong
pin fails earlier and differently.*

**A MISSING CREDENTIAL IS A RED RUN AND MAY NEVER DEGRADE TO "NOTHING TO PUSH".**
That shape — a mechanism reporting success for work it did not do — has been
sighted enough times in this repo to have its own rulings (100, 113, 159). The
empty-string case is the one that matters: **in GitHub Actions an unset secret
interpolates to `""`**, so a check that only tested for `undefined` would sail
straight past a missing repository secret.

**The proof is both directions, on a real repository, through the command line
the workflows actually run.** A guard that refuses everything passes a refusal
test on its own. A commit carrying `scripts/anything.mjs` alongside the snapshot
is refused with the path named and origin's `main` unmoved; the same commit
without it lands. Asserting against `classifyPushPaths` would have proved that
the code the fix introduced does what the code does (RULING 153) — the guard is
wired in the direct-invocation block, so that is where it is exercised.

**And it is verified against a case it was not derived from** (RULING 157). The
cutover was derived from `refresh-daily`. The independent case is `job-watch`,
independent in the way that matters rather than in name: the only profile whose
grant lies outside `data/`, the only one whose allowlist is a single exact file
rather than a directory prefix, and the only pusher whose commit is an alarm
rather than an artifact.

*Measured on adoption: 1 of 1 write-enabled deploy key; `pnpm protection:verify`
INTACT, 9 of 9, against the live API; 8 of 8 pushers plumbed; 46 guards passing
across the three affected test files.*

## RULING 166 — the body's own publication is rung one, and its bulk download is rung zero

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

- **amends** → `R-0084`
  - what changed: the ORDER INSIDE Tier A: the body's own publication is A0 and its bulk download is taken first, before A1 third-party compilations
  - what survives: RULING 84's three tiers stand and its cost-per-fact reasoning is untouched; it narrows nothing


(Adopted 2026-08-26, Sean's ruling, the sources-and-incumbency session. **Amends
RULING 84** under the RULING 99 procedure: RULING 84's three tiers stand and its
cost-per-fact reasoning is untouched, and what changes is the ORDER INSIDE
Tier A. Narrows nothing.)

**Before any aggregator, any third party, and any per-entity search, the
governing body that holds the office is walked first. Where that body offers a
bulk download, the bulk file is taken before any page-by-page retrieval. A
third-party source may only be reached after the body's own publication has been
walked and what it carries has been recorded.**

*Why this is being ruled now, stated plainly so it is not softened.* New
Hampshire's state legislative data reached this product through **LegiScan — a
third-party aggregator** — while the New Hampshire General Court publishes its
own data directly, at `gc.nh.gov/downloads/`, including a downloads section
carrying Member Data as `.txt`, `.xls` and `.xlsx` and an ODBC connection
document for a public read-only SQL Server. That page exists precisely so
consumers do not have to scrape the site. **The ladder was inverted.** LegiScan
is a good source and stays in use; it simply is not rung one, and reaching it
first meant no session ever asked what the body itself offered.

**This is not a legislature rule.** It applies to every body in the product — a
county, a school district, a city council, a state agency. The body that holds
the office publishes its own officeholders, and the bodies that publish in bulk
usually do so precisely to avoid being scraped.

**The amendment to RULING 84, stated exactly.** That ruling's Tier A is *broad
sources that answer many entities at once*, and its list mixes two kinds of
thing: government publications (the Census of Governments, NCES, the Secretary
of State, the county clerk) and third-party compilations (Wikipedia). Walked as
one tier, a session may reach an encyclopedia before it reaches the body the
encyclopedia is about. So Tier A splits:

- **Tier A0 — the body's own publication, and the tier above it in government.**
  Bulk download first, then the body's own pages. RULING 93's descend-the-
  hierarchy move lives here: a directory the tier above publishes about the tier
  below is the body's own publication about its subdivisions.
- **Tier A1 — third-party compilations that answer many entities at once.**
  Wikipedia, LegiScan, Citizens Count, Open States, GovTrack. Still Tier A,
  still cheap, still walked before Tier B and Tier C — and now walked AFTER A0.

Tier B (the entity's own official source, per entity) and Tier C (per-entity
search) are unchanged.

**A bulk file is rung zero because it is not a retrieval problem at all.** The
fourteen rungs in `CLAUDE.md` are about getting bytes past a wall. A published
`.txt` of the whole roster has no wall in front of it, and a session that walks
rungs 2 through 6 against a body's individual member pages while that file sits
one directory away has not been defeated by anything — it never asked.

*What it returned on the day it was adopted, measured rather than argued.*
`gc.nh.gov/downloads/Members.txt` is 82,694 bytes, 408 rows, tab-delimited, and
carries per legislator: name in three parts, chamber, seat number, county,
district, **`electedStatus`**, mailing address, phone, work email, party, title
and up to five committee assignments with their phone numbers. **406 of 408 rows
carry an email and 266 carry a phone** — two Kelly-standard fields for the whole
of the New Hampshire General Court, in one fetch, from the body itself.
`ftp://ftp.azsos.gov/cfsdata2/` — named in Arizona's own Bulk Filing Guide,
revised 28 July 2026 — is anonymous, live, and carries **8,828 Arizona campaign
committees** and the state's **109 campaign-finance filing jurisdictions**
(1 state, 15 counties, 93 cities and towns). Neither had ever been walked.

**And the ruling paid for itself twice over on adoption day**, which is the part
worth keeping. The brief that ordered this work named the NH public SQL Server
as `216.177.20.245\sqlexpress`. The body's own document at `gc.nh.gov` names
`66.211.150.69\sqlexpress`. Probed the same hour: the brief's address is
`ECONNREFUSED`, the body's answers with **TCP OPEN on 1433**. A session that had
gone to the aggregator, or to the brief, and not to the body, would have
recorded a dead endpoint.

<details>
<summary>The other hand-written copy of this rule, from <code>CLAUDE.md</code> — preserved verbatim</summary>

*Two copies of this rule were maintained by hand and they diverged. Neither was complete.
The fuller one is above; this is the other, kept whole rather than merged, because merging
prose neither author wrote would be composition.*

RULING 99 procedure: that ruling's three tiers stand and its cost-per-fact
reasoning is untouched. What changes is the ORDER INSIDE Tier A. It narrows
nothing.)

third-party source may only be reached after the body's own publication has been

**Tier A splits, and that split is the whole amendment.** **A0** is the body's

## RULING 167 — donor rendering is AGGREGATE ONLY, and no individual donor name or address renders anywhere

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/rendering-neutrality.md`.


(Adopted 2026-08-26, Sean's authority, stated in the sources-and-incumbency
brief as in force rather than as a proposal. It sits beside **RULING 126**,
which walls campaign-finance data out of everything sold; this governs what may
be shown to a READER, which is a different question and was open.)

**Totals, source types, in-state versus out-of-state, and employer-level
rollups. No individual donor name and no donor address renders anywhere in this
product, for FEC data or for state data.**

*The rationale stays attached, because a stripped rule reads as guidance.*
Publishing them is lawful — that is what a disclosure regime is — and this
product could render them and be within the law all day. **Rendering them
searchably builds a way to locate private individuals by their politics**, next
to a map, next to a zip box, in a product whose whole architecture is organised
around a reader's address. This project will not build that, and the reason is
not legal exposure.

The measurement that makes it concrete rather than hypothetical: the FEC's
individual-contribution schedule and New Hampshire's receipts file both carry
contributor **name, street address, city, state, zip, occupation and employer**,
and Arizona's Bulk Filing Guide (revised 28 July 2026) specifies the same seven
fields as columns 10 through 22 of every filed transaction — `Occupation` and
`Employer` are **conditionally REQUIRED** for individual contributions. Three
states' worth of the same personal record, arriving through three different
doors, is why this is a standing rule rather than a decision taken once per
source.

- **A donor is a private individual. A committee is not.** An organization
  renders as filed, with its registered name and committee type, exactly as the
  organizations-render-as-filed rule already requires. Nothing here narrows that.
- **An employer-level rollup is an aggregate and is permitted**; a single row
  that names one person's employer alongside their contribution is not, because
  with a name attached it is the same record wearing a summary's clothes.
- **This is a RENDER rule and not a COLLECTION rule.** The filings are retrieved
  and held with their provenance intact — a claim about money still needs its
  source record, and a source record we did not keep is a claim we cannot make.
  What is forbidden is putting an individual donor in front of a reader.
- **RULING 126 is untouched and is the other wall.** None of this data enters an
  export, an aggregate, or anything sold, whatever level it is summarised to.

*Audited on adoption across every funding surface, and the audit is the reason
this entry exists in the shape it does. **The session first wrote that nothing
rendered and the count changed was 0 of 0.** That was wrong, and it was wrong in
the way this repo names most often: it was an assertion about a surface nobody
had opened. `components/funding/funding-section.tsx` was rendering
`group.contributorName` beside `{group.city}, {group.state}` for every itemized
individual receipt in the snapshot, live, with `ripcord.fecContributorDisplay`
not pulled.*

***2 of 2 render sites changed.*** *The named one is the "Individual donors"
column. The second is the SECOND-HOP panel — a joint fundraiser's own book,
folded by a different call, concatenated into a different list, inside a
collapsed `<details>` — and it is the case a fix aimed at the first would have
left standing (RULING 103, RULING 157). Both now render*
`lib/funding/donor-privacy.ts`'s *aggregate: a donor count, a filing count, a
total, a state rollup that sums to it, and the candidate's own money held apart
as a subset. Guarded in* `tests/donor-aggregation.test.ts` *— 5 assertions, the
render half swept BY SHAPE with a planted violating component proving the sweep
catches a real one.*

*And the cheap fix was refused on purpose. Keeping the rows and dropping only
the names leaves an amount, a city and a date per row, which is re-identifiable
against the FEC's own public search in about a minute — the product would have
published the same record with one column hidden. The row had to stop being a
row.*

<details>
<summary>The other hand-written copy of this rule, from <code>CLAUDE.md</code> — preserved verbatim</summary>

*Two copies of this rule were maintained by hand and they diverged. Neither was complete.
The fuller one is above; this is the other, kept whole rather than merged, because merging
prose neither author wrote would be composition.*

(Adopted 2026-08-26, the author's authority, stated in the brief as in force
rather than as a proposal. It sits beside **RULING 126**, which walls

- **A donor is a private individual. A committee is not.** An organization

- **An employer-level rollup is an aggregate and is permitted**; a single row

## RULING 168 — Sean's ratification of the job-watch tracker grant, and his tracker decisions of that brief

*RATIFICATION · HISTORICAL · adopted 2026-08-26*

> **This is HISTORICAL.** It is history. It explains; it does not govern.


Recorded the way **RULING 161** recorded his decisions of 2026-08-26 and
**RULING 151** those of 2026-08-25 — so that a close has an authority which
exists, rather than a session deciding for him.

**`NH204` — RATIFIED IN FULL.** His words: the grant covers the complete
transaction, not one file.

*The reasoning he gave, recorded because a paraphrase of a decision is a
different decision.* `job-watch` opens a tracker row when a scheduled job fails
twice running, and **that row is the only channel telling him the alarms are
broken.** The row cannot reconcile unless its derived views are written with it.
The 2026-08-26 corruption happened precisely because the row landed and the
views did not.

**The enumerated set, verified against what the job actually writes rather than
against the list the brief supplied.** The brief named five paths and asked for
any difference to be reported. **There is none — 5 of 5 match**, and each is
already justified individually in `lib/ops/push-allowlist.ts`:

| Path | Why it is in the transaction |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/tracker-working.csv` | the row itself (`TRACKER_ROW_GRANT`) |
| `docs/tracker.md` | the readable view, regenerated in the same `tracker add` call |
| `docs/log.md` | the session-by-session record, same call |
| `docs/tracker-opened.json` | the opened-row ledger the guards reconcile against |
| `docs/tracker.xlsx` | the workbook Sean actually reads |

**Still barred outright, and this does not change:** `docs/rulings.md`, the
resolved tracker store, and every prefix in `NEVER_PUSHABLE` — `.github/`,
`scripts/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `components/`, `tests/`, `CLAUDE.md`. The grant is
enumerated paths only and **a path not named is refused**, checked twice by two
lists that are not derived from each other (RULING 147).

**The write is atomic** — row, session attribution, section state, derived
views, recount and reconciliation assertion, all or nothing. `scripts/tracker.mjs`
already refuses a whole batch rather than writing the good half of it, which is
the property this ratification depends on: a partial success is the defect the
grant exists to prevent, not merely to permit around.

*Also recorded from the same brief, so the close has an authority:* **`BAL-14`
is SETTLED** — width matching the *Would you vote for them?* box, green, in both
themes — and is not an open question. **`NS15`** closes on his authority: done,
communicated.

## RULING 169 — a walk is COUNTED or it did not happen

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.


Adopted 2026-08-26, the descent session, Item 3. Supersedes nothing. It is the
**operation-count rule** — *an operation that can return nothing must be asked
what it returned* — pointed at a SITE WALK rather than at an adapter, and it is
the instrument RULING 93 has never had.

**Coverage is built by DESCENDING the tiers of government in order, because each
tier publishes the tier beneath it. A tier is not complete until the tier above
has been asked what is in it. A body found only by per-entity search, when the
tier above publishes a list containing it, is a DEFECT IN THE WALK rather than a
find.**

**And every level's walk is REPORTED AS COUNTS: links found, links followed,
what each yielded, what was declined and why.** *"We walked the site"* without
those numbers is not a walk, and no report may claim one.

*The rationale stays attached, because a stripped rule reads as guidance, and
here the rationale is a diagnosis rather than an argument.*

RULING 93 has said *ask what the tier above publishes about the tier below*
since 2026-08-22. RULING 166 has said *the body's own publication is rung one*
since 2026-08-26. RULING 90 has said *exhaustion is argued, never asserted*.
None of them changed the behaviour, and the reason is that **not one of them
produces a number.** A session can satisfy all three in its own belief and be
graded identically to a session that walked one page — because the report shape
they produce is the same report shape.

Every session picked a body and hunted it. **No session had walked a tier top to
bottom**, and nothing in the process could tell the difference. That is RULING
88's diagnosis exactly, one level up: what changes behaviour is a required
output that cannot be produced by walking a list.

- **A count is per LEVEL, per STATE**, never one number for a run. A run total
  hides the level that returned nothing, which is the level somebody needed.
- **DECLINED carries its reason** — disallowed, off-scope, already recorded,
  unreachable — because a declined link and a followed link that yielded nothing
  are completely different facts, and a bare *followed* count runs them
  together.
- **The number that says whether the descent WORKED is bodies discovered that
  were not already in the registry.** Every other column measures effort.
- **The walk states its PASS COUNT and the final pass's new-link count. If the
  final pass found anything new, the walk was not finished and the session says
  so.** Following links produces more links; a walk that stops while its last
  pass was still producing has stopped, not finished.
- **Zero at a tier FAILS LOUDLY** (RULING 159). Zero counties in a US state is a
  broken walk, never a finding.

*What this does NOT license.* It is not a licence to count instead of hunting. A
high followed-count with no bodies discovered is a session that walked a site
thoroughly and learned nothing, and the report says that too.

<details>
<summary>The other hand-written copy of this rule, from <code>CLAUDE.md</code> — preserved verbatim</summary>

*Two copies of this rule were maintained by hand and they diverged. Neither was complete.
The fuller one is above; this is the other, kept whole rather than merged, because merging
prose neither author wrote would be composition.*

(Adopted 2026-08-26, Item 3. Supersedes nothing. It is the **operation-count
rule** — *an operation that can return nothing must be asked what it returned* —
pointed at a SITE WALK rather than at an adapter, and it is the instrument
RULING 93 has never had.)

**Coverage is built by DESCENDING the tiers of government in order, because each
tier publishes the tier beneath it. A tier is not complete until the tier above
has been asked what is in it. A body found only by per-entity search, when the
tier above publishes a list containing it, is a DEFECT IN THE WALK rather than a
find.**

**Every level's site is walked as a tree and the walk is REPORTED AS COUNTS:
links found, links followed, what each yielded, what was declined and why.**
*"We walked the site"* without those numbers is not a walk, and no report may
claim one.

*The rationale stays attached, because a stripped rule reads as guidance, and
here the rationale is a diagnosis rather than an argument.*

RULING 93 has said *ask what the tier above publishes about the tier below*
since 2026-08-22. RULING 166 has said *the body's own publication is rung one*.
RULING 90 has said *exhaustion is argued, never asserted*. Behaviour did not
change, and the reason is that **not one of them produces a number.** A session
can satisfy all three in its own belief and be graded identically to a session
that walked one page, because the report shape is the same either way.

Every session picked a body and hunted it. **No session had walked a tier top to
bottom**, and nothing in the process could tell the difference. That is RULING
88's diagnosis one level up: what changes behaviour is a required output that
cannot be produced by walking a list.

- **A count is per LEVEL, per STATE**, never one number for a run. A run total
  hides the level that returned nothing, which is the level somebody needed.
- **DECLINED carries its reason** — disallowed, off-scope, already recorded,
  unreachable. A declined link and a followed link that yielded nothing are
  completely different facts, and a bare *followed* count runs them together.
- **The number that says whether the descent WORKED is bodies discovered that
  were not already in the registry.** Every other column measures effort.
- **The walk states its PASS COUNT and the final pass's new-link count. If the
  final pass found anything new, the walk was not finished and the session says
  so.**
- **Zero at a tier FAILS LOUDLY** (RULING 159). Zero counties in a US state is a
  broken walk, never a finding.

*What this does NOT license.* It is not a licence to count instead of hunting. A
high followed-count with no bodies discovered is a session that walked a site
thoroughly and learned nothing, and the report says that too.

The machinery is `lib/hunt/descent.ts` and `pnpm descent`, guarded in
`tests/descent.test.ts`.

</details>

## RULING 170 — no number of attempts earns an absence, and a protocol that TERMINATES is not persistence

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

- **amends** → `R-0094`
  - what changed: what reaching the end of the five moves MEANS — running them does not earn an absence and never has; any cap in any brief is a FLOOR
  - what survives: RULING 94's five moves stand, its placement between Tier B and Tier C stands, and its void condition stands


Adopted 2026-08-26, the descent session, Item 9. **Amends RULING 94** under the
RULING 99 procedure. RULING 94's five moves stand, its placement between Tier B
and Tier C stands, and its void condition stands. What changes is what reaching
the end of them MEANS.

**RULING 94's five moves are the OPENING, not the count. Running them does not
earn an absence and never has.** An absence is earned only by the argument
RULING 90 requires.

**A session that has exhausted its ideas says "I have run out of ideas" — which
is a claim about the session — rather than "this is not published", which is a
claim about the government. Only one of those is ever true here.**

**Any cap in any brief — five moves, N routes, a list of seven — is a FLOOR.**
Reaching the end of a list is not completion. **A brief that appears to cap
effort is misdrafted, and the session says so rather than obeying the cap.**

*The rationale stays attached.* RULING 94 phrased its moves as five numbered
questions so they could not go stale, and the numbering was read as the job.
That is the same failure RULING 61 named about the manifest — *trying
thirty-seven routes and stopping does not tell you the forty-third would have
failed either* — arriving through the door built to prevent it. A protocol with
a terminating condition is a checklist, and a checklist completed is a session
that believes it complied.

**The standard, in the author's words: what would the most diligent, persistent
person do if they got stuck? Keep looking. Find another avenue.**

**And the productive question is not "where would this be published?" It is
"WHO WAS COMPELLED TO WRITE THIS DOWN?"** Governments are forced by statute to
produce documents nobody thinks of as directories — the municipal code that
establishes every board by ordinance, the tax rate table that must list every
levying district because somebody has to be billed, the legal notice published
in a newspaper of record, the budget and the audit, the minutes of the tier
above recording an appointment, the annual report, the state oversight
directory. **Those documents are where the dark bodies are**, and none of them
was in the ladder on the day this was adopted.

*This does not narrow RULING 144.* An argued absence may still be built from
walls, and it still expires the day a wall falls. What it forbids is arriving at
that argument by counting.

## RULING 171 — A BALLOT MEASURE IS DONE AT SEVEN FIELDS, AND THE MONEY IS A PAIR

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/rendering-neutrality.md`.


**A measure is DONE when it carries all seven, and there are no tiers of it:**

1. **The official text and official summary**, from the certifying body, cited.
2. **A plain-language decoding** — what it actually does, for a reader with no
   civic background. This is the product's founding promise.
3. **The household cost in units a person feels.** A sales-tax measure is a rate
   change; the reader wants dollars. A school override is a levy on assessed
   value; the reader wants what it does to their bill. **Where the body
   publishes an official fiscal estimate, cite it. Where it does not, say so —
   never estimate it ourselves.**
4. **Who certified it**, by what authority, and on what date it appears.
5. **The money FOR.**
6. **The money AGAINST.**
7. **A Sources section** to the same standard as a candidate card.

**EQUAL EFFORT FOR AND AGAINST IS CONSTITUTIONAL** and follows directly from
equal-effort-per-candidate. **Showing who funded the yes and not the no is
taking a side by omission.** Both sides ship at equal depth or neither ships,
and **the check REFUSES rather than reports** — a report of asymmetry is
something somebody reads after the asymmetric card has already been in front of
a reader.

**The vote-recommendation ban is unchanged.** No score, no ranking, no lean, no
aggregate. The household-cost field is a FACT ABOUT A BILL and never an argument
about it.

*The rationale stays attached, because a stripped rule reads as guidance.*

There is a definition of done for a CANDIDATE, enforced by `pnpm kelly` under
RULING 143. **There was none for a measure.** So the first measures to land
would have landed at whatever depth was convenient on the day, and **that depth
would have become the standard by default** — a standard nobody chose, set by
whichever measure happened to be easiest to research.

The measures are already real. Vail Unified has published an **Override
Reauthorization 2026** that does not appear at `85641`, and Pima County's
Propositions 418 and 419 were on a **March 2026** ballot. What was missing was
the definition, which is why this is adopted before the corpus exists rather
than after.

**Why a tiered standard was refused**, exactly as it was for candidates: a tier
tracks which measures had well-funded campaigns, which is the information
asymmetry the equal-effort rule exists to catch.

**Two states are findings about the world, and each carries a required
companion** — because an unsourced finding is an assertion, which is the thing
this product exists not to make:

- **`NONE_REGISTERED`** — this contest has no registered committee on this side.
  Legal only on the money fields, and only with **the filing officer named**. It
  is NEVER interchangeable with `NOT_HUNTED`; collapsing them would let a
  session skip the harder side and call it an absence.
- **`NO_OFFICIAL_ESTIMATE`** — the certifying body publishes no fiscal estimate.
  It carries **where we looked**, and it is the only honest answer for household
  cost in that case. This product does not estimate a household's bill itself:
  the never-generate-a-position rule, pointed at money.

**Two clocks, and the money's is the shorter.** Certified text does not change
after certification, so it carries the 14-day body-and-roster clock. Committee
filings move on statutory deadlines and a three-week-old contribution total
describes a different race, so the money carries the 7-day candidate-field
clock. **A presence expires as well as an absence** — one side going stale is
one side unshown, and it re-opens the asymmetry block automatically.

**`BLOCKED_ASYMMETRIC` is deliberately its own verdict** rather than a thinner
`OWED`. A measure missing its plain-language decoding needs MORE HUNTING; a
measure whose money is one-sided must NOT SHIP whatever else it carries. Those
are different instructions and one verdict cannot give both.

The machinery is `lib/hunt/measure-depth.ts` and `pnpm measures`, guarded in
`tests/measure-depth.test.ts` — whose load-bearing case is the one a report
could never enforce: **six of seven fields complete and one-sided money still
blocks.** The state is DERIVED and never stored, for RULING 116's reason: a
`measureDepth: "DONE"` column would go stale the moment any source moved and
nothing would notice.

*Measured on adoption:* the standard exists and **the corpus is empty**.
`pnpm measures` exits NON-ZERO and says so in words rather than printing a green
board about a population nobody has assembled — RULING 159's earned zero, named
at the moment it would have been most tempting to skip.

## RULING 172 — current authority and history are separate systems

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**History may explain current authority. History may never itself become
current authority merely because a session found an old paragraph.**

Two systems, not one file with two jobs. The canonical current answer to
"what governs now?" is compiled from typed records; the narrative that explains
why is retrieved on demand and is never loaded as default context.

*The rationale stays attached.* Sessions were reconstructing current law by
reasoning through chronology and supersession, and a session that reasons its
way to an answer can reason its way to a wrong one. A paragraph adopted in
August and replaced in August reads identically to one still in force — same
bold type, same adoption stamp, same confident voice. The only thing separating
them was a session noticing.

## RULING 173 — CLAUDE.md is the root constitution and carries current law only

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**`CLAUDE.md` contains CURRENT cross-cutting law only, plus the authority
hierarchy and the policy index.**

It does not contain superseded operative text, chronological ruling batches,
incident narratives whose purpose is historical, volatile counts, current
credential status, endpoint health, commit-specific measurements, or duplicated
full copies of domain law.

**Detailed current law lives in delegated domain policies** under
`docs/governance/policies/`. Superseded wording lives in history, never beside
the operative clause.

*What this is not.* It is not a size target met by deleting rationale. History
grows without a cap; what changes is that it stops being loaded as default
runtime context.

## RULING 174 — binding authority requires author provenance

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**Only `author_explicit` or `author_confirmed` provenance may create binding
law or decision state. An LLM may not upgrade its own confident prose into
"Sean ruled this."**

Four provenance kinds are kept apart: `author_explicit`, `author_confirmed`,
`session_interpretation`, `observed_fact`. A session's reading of a rule is
recorded as a reading. It does not become the rule by being written down
confidently.

**Where provenance cannot be established, the record says so and does not
bind.** Uncertainty is a legal state. Guessing is not.

## RULING 175 — supersession is structured data, and a partial amendment names both halves

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**A partial supersession must name what CHANGED and what SURVIVES. Do not
reduce a clause-level amendment to a boolean.**

Nine relation kinds are representable: `supersedes_full`, `supersedes_clause`,
`amends`, `extends`, `clarifies`, `implements`, `ratifies`, `derived_from`,
`related_to`.

*The rationale stays attached.* RULING 170 amends RULING 94 and says in its own
words that RULING 94's five moves stand, its placement stands, and its void
condition stands — three quarters of the rule is in force. A boolean
`superseded` destroys exactly that, and a session reading it would drop a rule
the amendment deliberately kept.

## RULING 176 — governance changes are atomic

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

- **amends** → `R-0099`
  - what changed: RULING 99's third clause — that an amendment adds a mapping line in BOTH docs/rulings.md and CLAUDE.md. That dual write is retired: docs/rulings.md is a GENERATED compatibility view and CLAUDE.md is a root constitution carrying current cross-cutting law only, so neither can receive a hand-written mapping line. An amendment now lands as a canonical event in docs/governance/ledger.jsonl, and every view regenerates from it
  - what survives: RULING 99's first two clauses in full — an amendment is a LATER DATED ruling that names the number it supersedes and states what changed and why. So does everything else it established: rulings are never edited in place and never silently dropped, a superseded ruling stays in the record marked superseded and carrying its successor, and adopted numbers are immutable and never renumbered to tidy a sequence

**A law or decision change is incomplete until the canonical event exists,
operative policy is updated where applicable, generated views are regenerated,
generated startup context is regenerated, and validation passes.**

**No state may ship where the constitution claims a ruling that the canonical
ledger does not contain.**

*Why this is law rather than a habit.* The hand-maintained dual write between
`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/rulings.md` is what let the constitution carry RULING 169
and RULING 170 while the ruling record stopped at 168. That specific mismatch is
RESOLVED — both files carry 169, 170 and 171 at the HEAD this was adopted
against, measured rather than assumed. **The mismatch was never the defect. The
architecture that permitted it was**, and a guard that only fixed the instance
would be the named-instance failure this repository names most often.

## RULING 177 — the subject universe may be bounded; the method never is

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

**THE UNIVERSE OF OWED SUBJECTS MAY BE BOUNDED. THE UNIVERSE OF METHODS IS
NOT. THE EFFORT PERMITTED TO COMPLETE AN OWED ITEM IS NOT ARBITRARILY CAPPED.**

This is the correction to two bad architectures at once.

**BAD:** try N things; N things failed; therefore absent.
**ALSO BAD:** follow every hyperlink forever; completion has no possible
boundary.

A current workstream may have a defined denominator. The discovery method
itself is permanently open-ended. **"Bounded universe" applies ONLY to the
subjects currently owed** — never to the method, the route manifest, the source
vocabulary, the platform vocabulary, the government-type vocabulary, or the
retrieval technique.

**A discovered route enlarges the active graph only when it plausibly advances
an owed question.** A government page does not recursively make every hyperlink
on the internet owed. That is what keeps this bounded without capping effort.

## RULING 178 — inherit everything, assume it is incomplete, keep the learning

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

**A method that works across 43 states is not "the method." It is the method
learned so far.**

If the repository knows 76 routes and those routes work across 43 states, that
means WE CURRENTLY KNOW 76 ROUTES. It does not mean THERE ARE 76 ROUTES. If the
next seven states require 11 more, the system learns those 11, records them,
classifies where they apply, and future sessions inherit all 87. Then 88. There
is no maximum.

- **A new route is PROJECT KNOWLEDGE, not session knowledge.** Every successful
  new avenue is persisted so another session never rediscovers it.
- **A failed inherited route is also knowledge.** It grows a sub-branch naming
  the jurisdictional shape it failed in and the date, and it is never deleted.
- **Every route carries applicability metadata.** Nationwide, state-specific,
  state-family, government-type, publisher, platform, document-type,
  jurisdiction, or **unknown portability — which is a VALID state.** Do not
  generalize farther than the evidence supports.
- **A NEW JURISDICTION IS PRESUMED CAPABLE OF TEACHING THE PROJECT A NEW
  METHOD.** "Nothing new learned" is a legitimate measured result only after
  genuine expansion work occurred. It may never be inferred merely because all
  inherited routes completed.
- **New knowledge reopens old conclusions.** When a route is learned, prior
  items recorded absent, blocked, dark or converged are identified
  MECHANICALLY, their exhaustion state is invalidated where the route applies,
  and they return to owed. This is structural, never something a future session
  is expected to remember.

**Inheritance is the STARTING advantage of a new state, never its constraint.**

## RULING 179 — convergence is versioned, and completion is derived from child state

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

**CONVERGED never means "we know every possible way to find this."** It means:
under the current project knowledge, for this defined universe, every currently
eligible avenue has a disposition as of this date.

Every convergence record states `convergedAsOf`, `methodVersion`,
`universeVersion` and `eligibleEdgeVersion`. **A newly applicable route, a
changed universe, or expired freshness reopens it.**

- **Item completion is DERIVED from child dispositions.** A model may not type
  "done" into a report while unresolved required children exist. The repository
  computes it.
- **A workstream is `COMPLETE_AS_OF` only when** its owed universe is defined,
  every member is accounted for exactly once, every required child has an
  allowed disposition, no UNKNOWN remains, no owed item is represented as absent
  because of a blocker, the eligible graph has converged for the current
  freshness window, and the completion is stamped with the method version it was
  earned under.
- **Graph convergence and factual absence are different.** A complete eligible
  pass finding zero new eligible routes does not mean there are no other sources
  on Earth.

## RULING 180 — session status, workstream status and graph status are three different facts

*LAW_DECISION · AMENDED · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**A session may run out of time. The work may remain open. Neither fact may
ever be misreported as "done" — and neither may be reported as a failure.**

Three independent axes:

    SESSION:    CLEAN_HANDOFF | COMPLETE | FAILED_CLOSEOUT
    WORKSTREAM: OPEN | COMPLETE_AS_OF <date>
    GRAPH:      EXPANDING | CONVERGED_AS_OF <date>

**An ended context window with every byte persisted and an exact cursor is
`SESSION: CLEAN_HANDOFF` / `WORKSTREAM: OPEN`. That is SUCCESS.** Lost or
unrepresented remainder is failure.

**The repository, not the model, generates the handoff.** Close-out tooling
produces the exact cursor and the exact unresolved set from canonical
work-state. The model may explain it; it may not invent it. No "the rest", no
omitted tail.

## RULING 181 — a frontier is state, not a recipe for recreating state

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

**The canonical store persists every discovered eligible edge with a stable
id, its parent/source provenance, and its disposition. Processed and queued
edges are explicit. The current cursor is explicit.**

**Restart does not require recrawling seeds to discover what was already
known.** A seed list may INITIALIZE a new workstream; it may not be the only
source from which an in-progress workstream reconstructs what remains.

**`passes` and `budget` are execution controls. They choose HOW MUCH queued
work to process. They never define WHAT WORK EXISTS.**

A derived frontier index may be regenerated from canonical edge state. If
canonical outstanding work exists only because a future crawl will rediscover
it, it is not persisted.

## RULING 182 — permission state and transport state are orthogonal

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/sources-licensing.md`.

**A permission decision and the ability to retrieve the permission document
are different facts, and the system may never collapse them.**

    PERMISSION: ALLOWED | DISALLOWED | CANNOT_TELL | NOT_APPLICABLE
    TRANSPORT:  REACHABLE | FAILED_AT_RUNG | CHALLENGED | TIMEOUT
                | TLS_CLIENT_MISMATCH | OTHER_NAMED_FAILURE

**"could not fetch robots.txt with this client" is NEVER "robots disallows this
host."**

- Fail safe for the ROUTE where permission genuinely cannot be established —
  `CANNOT_TELL` refuses the fetch, exactly as RULING 148 requires.
- **Do not convert transport failure into `DISALLOWED`.**
- **Continue alternate compliant retrieval methods for the permission
  document**, and continue alternate compliant branches to the underlying
  public fact.
- Freshness and recheck still apply.

*The rationale stays attached.* The descent session found a transport failure
while reading permission being interpreted as permission being unanswerable,
which then refused the host. Escalating the retrieval client recovered multiple
hosts — including the tops of two state descents. **A blocked route may never
become a blocked fact.**

## RULING 183 — a lead is not a body

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

**A link detector or site walker produces CANDIDATES. Coverage increases only
through verified and promoted bodies.**

    EDGE_DISCOVERED -> ENTITY_CANDIDATE -> ENTITY_VERIFIED -> BODY_PROMOTED

with alternate endings `DUPLICATE`, `REJECTED_FALSE_POSITIVE`,
`NEEDS_CLASSIFICATION`. The transition and its evidence are persisted.

**A report may state all counts. NO CANDIDATE COUNT MAY SUBSTITUTE FOR THE
PROMOTED-BODY COUNT**, and RULING 169's load-bearing number is unchanged:
bodies discovered that were not already in the registry.

**Detector counts require calibration against what the detector actually
found.** A job board produced 154 false candidates and a calendar view produced
214. Detectors report promoted, rejected and uncertain outcomes; tests include
false-positive calibration rather than merely non-zero output. **A detector must
not be able to satisfy a success threshold entirely with known false
positives.**

## RULING 184 — blocked is a real state, and a finite attempt count never earns absence

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

- **extends** → `R-0170`

**Delete the false binary `taken OR absent`.** Source and work dispositions
represent at least: `UNWALKED`, `DISCOVERED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `INGESTED`,
`POINTER_ONLY`, `WALKED_NO_YIELD`, `BLOCKED_CURRENTLY`,
`REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER`, `RECORDS_REQUEST_PENDING`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`,
`RECHECK_DUE`.

A CAPTCHA is not absence. Missing tooling is not absence. A pending records
request is not absence. A third-party pointer is not necessarily something to
ingest. A presently prohibited route is not absence.

**Five moves, seven tiers, N routes, every manifest entry, every known branch —
these are FLOORS and instruments. Reaching their end never means "therefore the
information does not exist."**

If a session has no further avenue it says **"I have run out of ideas"**, which
is a claim about the session. It is never "the government does not publish
this", which is a claim about a government.

## RULING 185 — the authority precedence model

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**One precedence model, documented, and it is this one:**

1. Explicit current author directive.
2. Root constitution (`CLAUDE.md`).
3. Delegated current policy for the relevant domain.
4. Active current non-law author decision.
5. Session brief / tracker scope instruction.
6. Operational state / current measurements.
7. Historical ledger and history views.

**History explains. History does not override.**

**A brief that conflicts with current law does not silently win** unless it is
an explicit author amendment. The conflict is REPRESENTED rather than resolved
by whichever document the session happened to read last.

## RULING 186 — a session opens on task-relevant current authority, never on the full history

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**`pnpm governance:open --task <domain>` loads the root constitution, the
applicable current domain policies, the applicable active current decisions,
unresolved governance conflicts, the governance snapshot hash, and pointers to
current tracker and work state.**

**It does NOT dump the historical ledger as normal startup context.**
Historical rationale is retrieved on demand.

For long-running work, opening also prints canonical workstream and method
state: workstream status, graph status, method version, routes inherited and
applicable, the exact resume cursor, and the counts of open, blocked and
recheck-due children.

**If answering a current-rule question still requires reading 80,000 words of
chronology, this rule is not being met.**

## RULING 187 — a well-preserved handoff is not automatically a legitimate stop

*LAW_DECISION · SUPERSEDED · adopted 2026-08-26*

> **This is SUPERSEDED.** It is history. It explains; it does not govern.

- **amends** → `R-0180`
  - what changed: the session-status vocabulary expands from three values to five, and a measured stop accounting is required at every non-COMPLETE close
  - what survives: RULING 180's separation of session, workstream and graph status; that the repository generates the handoff; that item completion is derived from child state; and that lost or unrepresented remainder is failure

**There are TWO independent questions at session close: was the state
preserved correctly, and was there a legitimate reason to stop? A session may
preserve everything perfectly and still stop too early.**

    SESSION: COMPLETE
             CLEAN_HANDOFF_LIMIT_REACHED
             CLEAN_HANDOFF_EXTERNAL_STOP
             EARLY_HANDOFF_WITH_CAPACITY
             FAILED_CLOSEOUT

Every non-`COMPLETE` close records **measured** `context_used_percent`,
`context_remaining_percent`, a specific `stop_reason`, and
`executable_owed_work_remaining`. Where the environment exposes context usage
directly, that reading is used rather than inferred.

**`CLEAN_HANDOFF_LIMIT_REACHED`** requires ALL of: canonical state fully
persisted; exact cursor and remainder generated from it; executable owed work
remaining; productive authorized work continued to a real context boundary; AND
either **at least 80% of usable context actually consumed**, or the platform
reporting an imminent context limit, compaction event or hard stop.

**THE 80% FIGURE IS A FLOOR FOR THAT STATUS. IT IS NOT A TARGET.** It is a
defect to consume context merely to qualify for a clean handoff — no repeating
analysis, no restating recorded work, no unnecessary prose, no low-value
busywork, no delayed correct action, no enlarged reports. **If productive
executable work remains, do that work.**

**`CLEAN_HANDOFF_EXTERNAL_STOP`** may be used with substantial context
remaining only when an actual external condition prevents continued authorized
work — the author says stop, the environment terminates the run, or every
remaining executable item is blocked externally and the brief holds nothing else
to skip forward to. **One blocked item does not qualify if other authorized work
exists. Skip forward.**

**`EARLY_HANDOFF_WITH_CAPACITY` is REQUIRED** when substantial usable context
remains, executable authorized work remains, no qualifying external stop exists,
and the session closes anyway. The work may be perfectly persisted and the
cursor perfect. It is still an early stop. **Do not convert preservation quality
into permission to stop.**

**`COMPLETE` means the authorized work actually satisfies its completion
rules.** Finishing the current checklist is not sufficient if the standing queue
requires the session to continue; finishing one phase is not sufficient if the
workstream remains owed. **The model does not award itself `COMPLETE`. The
state does.**

*Applied to the preceding descent session, from the evidence rather than by
automatic translation:* it shed more than half its visual work at approximately
56% context, with executable brief items remaining and no qualifying external
stop. Its persistence and handoff were genuinely strong and that remains a
positive fact. Its migrated semantic state is nonetheless
**`EARLY_HANDOFF_WITH_CAPACITY` / `OPEN` / `EXPANDING`**. Its historical
report is not rewritten.

The machinery is `classifySessionStop` in `lib/workstate/types.ts`, guarded
in `tests/stopping-legitimacy.test.ts` — whose load-bearing case is the one
prose could never enforce: **a session claiming
`CLEAN_HANDOFF_LIMIT_REACHED` at 56% is REFUSED, and the refusal names what
was claimed.**

## RULING 188 — the descent freezes only for the minimum safe state cutover

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-26*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**FREEZE THE MOVING STATE ONLY LONG ENOUGH TO REPLACE ITS CANONICAL
STORE. DO NOT FREEZE THE PRODUCT UNTIL EVERY HISTORICAL DOCUMENT IS PERFECT.**

An active discovery frontier must not keep changing while its canonical state
representation is being replaced. It does not follow that the work stops until
the whole governance history is normalized — that would spend an extended period
building the system that DESCRIBES the work instead of doing the work.

**Stage 1** is the minimum safe cutover, and its acceptance list is a SAFETY
list: the ruling ledger imported with immutable ids and resolving aliases; new
decisions landing through one atomic path; the rulings document needing no
hand-maintained second write; current discovery law and current
shipping/verification/close-out law each compiled to one authoritative surface;
the active frontier migrated to machine-readable state with stable edge ids,
queued and processed edges, an exact cursor, parent provenance and dispositions;
candidates separate from promoted bodies; permission separate from transport;
cumulative method knowledge preserved and inherited; the handoff generated from
canonical state; the Stage 1 validators passing; and a resume proof showing the
frontier continues **without rediscovering outstanding edges from seeds**.

**When those pass, the freeze is LIFTED and the descent resumes immediately.**

**Stage 2 does NOT hold the freeze.** Full historical type classification, full
provenance normalization, complete supersession normalization, every remaining
domain policy, final root reduction, remaining historical ambiguity and
compatibility-path removal all continue afterwards, while the live work benefits
from the new architecture.

**THERE IS NO SECOND MIGRATION OF THE ACTIVE FRONTIER.** From the cutover
forward, new descent work writes directly into the canonical frontier, new
methods into the cumulative store, new decisions through the atomic governance
transaction, and new convergence states under the versioned model.

**A freeze that outlasts its safety reason is reported as a blocker with the
exact failing criterion named.** "Migration incomplete" is not an acceptable
substitute for naming which criterion failed.

The gate is `pnpm stage1`, guarded in `tests/stopping-legitimacy.test.ts`,
which fails if Stage 1 ever gates on Stage 2 work.

## RULING 189 — a session does not measure its own context, and stops for real reasons only

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-27*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

- **supersedes_full** → `R-0187`
  - what changed: the entire context-usage stopping model is removed — context_used_percent, context_remaining_percent, the 80% floor, the platform-limit signal, CLEAN_HANDOFF_LIMIT_REACHED and EARLY_HANDOFF_WITH_CAPACITY all go, because the session cannot measure the quantity they were built on
  - what survives: that a well-preserved handoff is not automatically a legitimate stop; that the two questions at close are independent; that the model does not award itself a status and a claim the state refuses is named; that COMPLETE is derived from owed work; and that an external stop must be real, one blocked item never qualifying while other authorized work exists
- **amends** → `R-0180`
  - what changed: the session-status vocabulary is COMPLETE | CLEAN_HANDOFF_AUTHOR_STOP | CLEAN_HANDOFF_EXTERNAL_STOP | EARLY_HANDOFF | FAILED_CLOSEOUT, and the stop accounting recorded at close carries no measurement of context
  - what survives: RULING 180's separation of session, workstream and graph status; that the repository generates the handoff and the model may not invent it; that item completion is derived from child state; and that lost or unrepresented remainder is failure

**A SESSION DOES NOT MEASURE ITSELF. The context-usage stopping model is
REMOVED — every percentage, every threshold, and every proxy for one.**

RULING 187 required a session to record `context_used_percent` and
`context_remaining_percent` at every non-`COMPLETE` close, and gave one
status an **80% floor**. The model does not possess that measurement. A
session reported approximately **4% used / 96% remaining** while the
interface it was running inside displayed a context gauge at roughly **47%**.
The classifier believed the number, because a number was all it was given.

**A guessed quantity dressed as a measurement is worse than no quantity.** It
made a status that reads as success purchasable with an estimate, and it gave
a session a standing reason to reason about its own capacity instead of about
the work.

**The operating rule, entire:**

    DO THE WORK THAT WAS ASKED FOR.
    KEEP WORKING WHILE AUTHORIZED EXECUTABLE WORK REMAINS.
    STOP WHEN THE REQUESTED WORK IS ACTUALLY COMPLETE, WHEN THE AUTHOR
    EXPLICITLY STOPS OR REDIRECTS THE SESSION, OR WHEN THE ENVIRONMENT
    ITSELF ACTUALLY PREVENTS CONTINUATION.

**A session does not estimate context used, estimate context remaining,
narrate approximate percentages, monitor its own context as a work-management
signal, stop because a threshold is thought to be reached, or classify itself
as early on guessed capacity.** Nor is the percentage replaced by another
arbitrary proxy — elapsed minutes, token guesses, message counts, command
counts, commit counts, subjective fatigue, or a work quota. **It is a defect
to consume context or produce prose in order to cross any threshold, and
there is now no threshold to cross.**

**The five statuses, replacing RULING 187's five:**

    SESSION: COMPLETE
             CLEAN_HANDOFF_AUTHOR_STOP
             CLEAN_HANDOFF_EXTERNAL_STOP
             EARLY_HANDOFF
             FAILED_CLOSEOUT

Every non-`COMPLETE` close records a specific `stop_reason`, whether the
AUTHOR stopped the session, whether an ACTUAL external condition prevented
continuing, and `executable_owed_work_remaining` — which is DERIVED from
canonical state, never asserted. **No percentage is recorded and none is
asked for.**

**`CLEAN_HANDOFF_EXTERNAL_STOP` is never INFERRED.** One blocked item does
not qualify while other authorized work exists — skip forward.

**MERGE CADENCE IS NOT SESSION CADENCE.** RULING 1 governs shipping: verify
locally, accumulate the session's work, ship once at the real end. **The fact
that the planned merge has occurred is not a legitimate reason to stop**, and
the normal answer is to DELAY the merge until the session is actually ready
to end. The preceding descent session stopped on `one planned merge per
session (RULING 1), now taken` while executable work remained; that is the
wrong reading, and it is now refused mechanically. Any author-directed
mid-session merge exception already in force is preserved.

**PERSISTED RESUMABILITY IS NOT PERMISSION TO STOP VOLUNTARILY.** Canonical
workstate, exact frontier persistence, exact resume cursors, unmaterialized-
obligation accounting, generated handoffs, method knowledge, the state corpus
and durable closeout records are all UNCHANGED and undiminished. They exist
so that an interrupted session can be resumed. They are not a licence to end
one.

The machinery is `classifySessionStop` and `NON_REASONS` in
`lib/workstate/types.ts`, guarded in `tests/stopping-legitimacy.test.ts`.
**A stated stop reason that appeals to self-estimated capacity or to merge
cadence cannot make a stop clean: it is refused, and the refusal names the
non-reason it appealed to.**

## RULING 190 — a session is an engineering organization, not one serial developer

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-28*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/meta-governance.md`.

**WHEN TWO OR MORE AUTHORIZED EXECUTABLE WORKSTREAMS ARE MATERIALLY
INDEPENDENT, SAFE PARALLEL EXECUTION IS THE DEFAULT. Serializing independent
work is a process defect that must name the dependency it was avoiding.**

The author states desired product outcomes. The session diagnoses, decomposes,
delegates, executes, integrates and ships. That division is the whole rule: a
session that receives twelve outcomes and runs them single-file has converted an
engineering organization into a ticket queue, and the conversion is invisible in
the report because a serial log reads exactly like a parallel one that finished.

**Before broad implementation, every session:**

    1  loads current governance for the task;
    2  identifies the authorized executable work universe;
    3  constructs a dependency and conflict graph;
    4  identifies the independent workstreams;
    5  fans them out using the strongest supported parallel mechanism;
    6  designates one integration and release owner;
    7  keeps independent streams progressing while another waits or blocks.

The decomposition is PROPORTIONAL. Two five-line edits to one file are one
workstream, and inventing branches for them is the same defect wearing the
opposite costume.

**The invariants.**

    INDEPENDENT WORK              -> PARALLEL BY DEFAULT
    TRUE DEPENDENCY               -> SERIALIZE AND NAME WHY
    ONE WORKSTREAM BLOCKED        -> THE OTHERS CONTINUE
    ONE WORKSTREAM DONE           -> READY_FOR_INTEGRATION, NOT SESSION DONE
    TRACKER ROW CREATED           -> NOT WORK COMPLETION
    LARGE PR / MANY FILES         -> NOT A STOP REASON
    P0                            -> START AND PRIORITIZE IMMEDIATELY,
                                     NEVER FREEZE INDEPENDENT ENGINEERS

**A tracker row is a record of work, never a substitute for it.** A session that
opens a row for work it could execute now has not delegated the work; it has
deferred it, and RULING 189 already says what a voluntary stop with owed work is
called.

**The law is environment-portable and names no vendor.** The obligation is to
use the STRONGEST PARALLEL MECHANISM THE ENVIRONMENT ACTUALLY SUPPORTS —
subagents or parallel agents where they exist, otherwise worktrees, branches,
concurrent shells and processes, parallel public-source retrieval and parallel
test or research jobs. Where only one execution thread genuinely exists, the
obligation survives as interleaving: advance another stream on every wait rather
than finishing whole domains in the order they were listed. "I cannot spawn
another engineer" is not a dependency, and neither is any other statement about
tooling.

**A subagent's report of "done" is not inspection.** The lead owns truth,
coordination, conflict resolution and full-product validation regardless of what
a delegated branch claims.

**CORRECTNESS STILL OUTRANKS SPEED, and this rule extends rather than touches
"correct first, fast second, nothing third."** The goal is MAXIMUM SAFE PARALLEL
THROUGHPUT, never the maximum number of branches. Two branches independently
rewriting one canonical store, or independently regenerating one generated
output, are refused by this rule rather than permitted by it: that is not
concurrency, it is data loss with two authors.

**The instrument is `pnpm orchestration:check`**, over the session plan in
`data/workstate/orchestration/`, and it derives the verdict rather than
accepting one. Each workstream records its id, its dependency ids and the reason
for each, the conflict domain it owns as paths and data, the artifacts it
produces and consumes, whether it is executable, and its disposition. **A
declared dependency is PROVEN only by a mechanical fact** — an owned-domain
overlap, or an artifact one workstream produces and another consumes. An edge
backed by prose alone is reported UNPROVEN and never silently accepted.
Independent, executable and serialized with nothing checkable behind it is a
FAILURE, named pair by pair.

**The refused justifications, because each has already been used here:** PR or
diff size, branch simplicity, conflict avoidance, convenience, tidiness,
unspecified caution, priority mistaken for a lock, and the absence of subagents.
None of them is a dependency.

**What this instrument cannot do is stated rather than hidden.** Wall-clock
concurrency is not observable from this repository — nothing records when a
branch's work actually ran, and a session cannot stamp a reliable clock. So the
guard checks the SHAPE OF THE PLAN and the JUSTIFICATION OF EVERY SERIALIZATION,
which are the two things written down. Recorded concurrency evidence —
worktrees, branches, agent ids — is corroboration, reported and never scored.

## RULING 191 — one integration owner, one combined head, one merge at the end

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-28*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/shipping-ci.md`.

- **extends** → `R-0190`

**A COMPLETED BRANCH IS NOT A COMPLETED SESSION.** RULING 190 fans the work
out; this is what the work comes back to.

**ONE INTEGRATION OWNER.** Exactly one branch owns canonical truth, the shared
governance artifacts, integration, combined verification and the final ship.
Parallel workstreams own their code, their tests and their own source data —
they do NOT each edit the shared stores. Canonical work state, the tracker
stores and workbook, the session state and log, the method store, and any
generated governance or canonical output are reconciled ONCE, by the integration
owner, in sequence.

**A branch changes canonical INPUTS. The integration owner regenerates the
OUTPUT once.** Letting each branch regenerate and commit a competing full-file
version of one generated artifact manufactures a conflict out of nothing and
violates RULING 92 on the way past.

**Shared load-bearing application files are decided BEFORE the fan-out, not
discovered after it.** Where two streams both need one such file, the session
picks deliberately: they are really one workstream; or one exposes an interface
the other depends on; or they modify separate regions and the ownership is
recorded. Discovering the dependency only after both branches contain broad
rewrites is the failure this clause exists to prevent.

**A workstream finishing means READY_FOR_INTEGRATION.** It does not merge to
`main`. Sub-workstream branches are implementation vehicles; the default
shipping topology is one final integrated PR from the integration branch.

**Branch-local green is necessary and not sufficient. Only the integrated head
is the product that ships.** After every integration, the focused overlap tests
for the stream just integrated run again; after all of them, the full local gate
set, the production build, the reader-visible controls, the source-denominator
checks and the generated-output checks run on the combined head — including the
interactions BETWEEN workstreams, which is the only place a combined head can
fail that no branch could.

**Where two branches conflict, neither "ours" nor "theirs" is an answer.** Both
branches were preserving an invariant. The integration owner re-reads both and
produces the combined behaviour.

This changes nothing about WHEN a merge happens. RULING 1 stands: verify
locally, accumulate, ship once at the real end, and the merge waits until the
session is ready to end rather than the session ending because the merge
happened.

## RULING 192 — method knowledge is typed by claim class, and a false conclusion never deletes a valid route

*LAW_DECISION · ACTIVE · adopted 2026-08-28*

> Operative current text: `docs/governance/policies/discovery.md`.

**Method knowledge is inherited by every later session and none of them
re-derives it, so a wrong sentence in the store costs every session after it and
arrives PRE-ARGUED.** Every assertion the store makes is one of four declared
classes:

    A  ROUTE_EXISTENCE     this public route exists
    B  ROUTE_OUTCOME       it yielded / zeroed / failed / was blocked, in X, on Y
    C  COVERAGE_CLAIM      it appears complete or incomplete for a field or class
    D  DERIVED_CONCLUSION  the public record universe contains, or does not contain, X

**1. A FALSE C OR D MAY NEVER DELETE A VALID A.** Withdrawing a coverage claim
or a derived conclusion never retires, narrows or removes the route it rested
on, and never touches the outcome it was read off. The route keeps inheriting.

*This is the Pima case, and it is why the rule is structural rather than
advisory.* The false entry was not a bad route. It was a VALID route, whose
existence and whose measured outcome were both correct, carrying a false
conclusion in the same paragraph at the same authority. With one undifferentiated
blob per route the only available moves are to rewrite the paragraph or delete
the route — and **a deleted route is one a later session rediscovers as new**.
So each assertion carries its own record and its own retraction.

**2. C AND D REQUIRE STRUCTURED PROVENANCE AND A STATED VALIDATION STATE** — the
artifact, the route disposition that produced the observation, the jurisdictions
and vendors it covers, and the date from `pnpm stamp`. **A coverage claim or a
derived conclusion may not become inherited authority merely because the worker
who wrote it believed it.** A and B do not require it: the id is the route, and
an outcome already carries its jurisdiction and its date. `UNVALIDATED` is a
permitted state; SILENCE is not, because silence reads to a later session as
though the claim had been checked.

**3. A WITHDRAWAL MECHANICALLY FLAGS ITS DEPENDENTS.** Every assertion declares
what it rests on, BY ID. Retraction, supersession, correction or reopening
surfaces every assertion that named it, and a dependent that is neither withdrawn
nor revalidated since is a VALIDATION FAILURE rather than a note somebody might
read. **Dependence is declared, never inferred from text** — a text match between
